Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Venturia inaequalis, spreads in cool wet spring weather
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit
Apple___Apple_scab.remedy: Apply a protectant fungicide (e.g. captan or myclobutanil) at green tip stage and repeat every 7-10 days during wet periods. Remove and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to cut overwintering spores.
Apple___Apple_scab.urgency: Treat within a week to prevent spread

Apple___Black_rot.cause: Botryosphaeria obtusa, enters through wounds and dead wood
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered leaf spots, rotting fruit with concentric rings
Apple___Black_rot.remedy: Prune out dead/cankered wood and mummified fruit. Apply fungicide (captan/thiophanate-methyl) starting at pink bud stage. Improve air circulation via pruning.
Apple___Black_rot.urgency: Remove infected material immediately to stop spread

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae, requires nearby juniper/cedar host
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on leaves, tube-like structures on fruit
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.remedy: Apply fungicide (myclobutanil) from pink bud through several weeks after petal fall. Remove nearby juniper/cedar trees if feasible, or plant rust-resistant apple varieties.

Apple___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring, balanced fertilization, and standard irrigation schedule.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Xanthomonas spp., spreads via splashing water and contaminated tools
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that turn scabby
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.remedy: Apply copper-based bactericide combined with mancozeb. Avoid overhead irrigation, avoid working in fields when plants are wet, and rotate crops for 2 years away from solanaceous plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.urgency: Act before spots coalesce and defoliation begins

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Alternaria solani, favored by warm humid conditions
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric 'target-spot' brown rings on lower/older leaves first
Tomato___Early_blight.remedy: Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or mancozeb) every 7-10 days. Remove lower infected leaves, mulch to prevent soil splash, stake plants for airflow, and rotate crops.
Tomato___Early_blight.urgency: Treat within a few days to protect fruiting stage

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans, spreads extremely fast in cool wet weather
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large irregular water-soaked grey-green lesions, white fuzzy growth on leaf undersides
Tomato___Late_blight.remedy: This spreads fast and can destroy a field in days. Apply a systemic fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil + metalaxyl or a copper-based product) immediately. Remove and destroy infected plants. Avoid overhead watering.
Tomato___Late_blight.urgency: URGENT: treat same day, isolate/remove infected plants to protect the rest of the field

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Passalora fulva, thrives in high humidity (common in greenhouses)
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surface, olive-green mold underneath
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.remedy: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity. Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or copper-based). Avoid wetting foliage when watering.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.urgency: Treat within a week, mainly a humidity management issue

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Septoria lycopersici, spreads via water splash
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and grey centers, tiny black specks in center
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.remedy: Remove infected lower leaves, apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or mancozeb), mulch soil, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.urgency: Treat before it spreads to upper canopy

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Tetranychus urticae, thrives in hot dry conditions
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves, fine webbing, leaf bronzing
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.remedy: Spray with insecticidal soap or miticide (abamectin). Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) if available. Increase humidity around plants to discourage mites.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.urgency: Treat within a few days before population explodes

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Corynespora cassiicola, favored by warm humid weather
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings, similar to early blight but on both leaves and fruit
Tomato___Target_Spot.remedy: Apply fungicide (azoxystrobin or chlorothalonil), improve air circulation via pruning/staking, avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling, yellowing leaves, stunted growth, reduced fruit
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.remedy: No cure once infected - remove and destroy infected plants to stop spread. Control whitefly vector with insecticide or yellow sticky traps. Use virus-resistant tomato varieties next season.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.urgency: URGENT: remove infected plants immediately, target whiteflies to protect healthy plants

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Highly contagious virus spread by contact, tools, hands, seeds
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light/dark green leaves, leaf distortion, stunted growth
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.remedy: No chemical cure - remove and destroy infected plants. Disinfect tools with 10% bleach solution between plants. Wash hands before handling plants. Use certified virus-free seed next season.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.urgency: Remove infected plants promptly to prevent field-wide spread

Tomato___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring, balanced fertilization, and standard irrigation schedule.

Potato___Early_blight.cause: Alternaria solani, favored by warm humid weather, stressed plants
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark concentric-ring spots on older leaves first
Potato___Early_blight.remedy: Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or mancozeb) on a 7-10 day schedule. Ensure balanced nitrogen fertilization (both excess and deficiency increase susceptibility), rotate crops.

Potato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans - the pathogen behind the Irish Potato Famine, spreads very fast in cool wet weather
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves, white mold on undersides, rapid plant collapse
Potato___Late_blight.remedy: Apply systemic fungicide immediately (metalaxyl + mancozeb/chlorothalonil). Destroy infected plants and tubers. Do not compost infected material. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Potato___Late_blight.urgency: URGENT: same-day treatment, this can wipe out the entire field within days

Potato___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring and standard care.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Puccinia sorghi, favored by cool moist weather
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.remedy: Apply fungicide (azoxystrobin or propiconazole) if infection appears before tasseling. Plant rust-resistant hybrids. Usually minor if it appears late in season.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.urgency: Monitor; treat only if severe before tasseling

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Exserohilum turcicum, favored by moderate temps and high humidity
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green lesions on leaves
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.remedy: Apply fungicide (strobilurin or triazole class) if detected before tasseling and conditions favor spread. Rotate crops, use resistant hybrids, till under crop residue.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.urgency: Treat within a week if disease is spreading up the canopy

Corn_(maize)___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring and standard care.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Guignardia bidwellii, favored by warm wet spring weather
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots, fruit shrivels into hard black mummies
Grape___Black_rot.remedy: Apply fungicide (mancozeb or myclobutanil) starting at bud break through several weeks post-bloom. Remove mummified fruit and infected canes during dormant pruning.
Grape___Black_rot.urgency: Treat before bloom to protect developing fruit

Grape___healthy.remedy: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring and standard care.
